entities.name: Behistun Inscription
entities.label: Evidence
entities.summary: A monumental multilingual inscription carved c. 520 BCE on a cliff face in western Iran by order of Achaemenid King Darius I. Written in Old Persian, Elamite, and Babylonian cuneiform, it records Darius's rise to power and was crucial to the decipherment of cuneiform script by Henry Rawlinson (1835–1847), unlocking the entire field of Assyriology and Mesopotamian studies.
